title: Water pumped into and drained from a tank

stimulus.title: Water pumped into and drained from a tank
stimulus.text: Water is pumped into a tank at a rate modeled by $E(t) = 50 + 30\sin\left(\frac{t^2}{40}\right)$ liters per hour, and water drains from the tank at a rate modeled by $D(t) = 15 + 9t$ liters per hour, for $0 \le t \le 10$ hours. At time $t = 0$ the tank holds 200 liters. The graph shows both rates.

plot.label: Graphs of the pumping rate E(t) and the draining rate D(t), in liters per hour, for t from 0 to 10 hours; the curves cross once near t = 7

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many liters of water are pumped into the tank from $t = 0$ to $t = 10$ hours?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Is the amount of water in the tank increasing or decreasing at time $t = 6$ hours? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: Compares $E(6)$ and $D(6)$ (or finds the sign of $E(6) - D(6)$)
Increasing, because $E(6) > D(6)$: water enters faster than it drains
accept: "$A'(6) = E(6) - D(6) > 0$, so the amount is increasing"

parts.sample: $E(6) - D(6) \approx 73.500 - 69 = 4.500 > 0$. Water is pumped in faster than it drains at $t = 6$, so the amount of water in the tank is increasing.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write an expression involving one or more integrals that gives the amount of water $A(t)$, in liters, in the tank at time $t$.

rubric.point: An integral of $E - D$ from 0 to $t$

accept: an expression with 200 + ... and the correct integral

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the absolute maximum amount of water in the tank for $0 \le t \le 10$. Justify your answer.

accept: a table of the three candidates (endpoints and the critical point)

parts.sample: $A'(t) = E(t) - D(t) = 0$ when $t = c \approx 7.041$ (calculator). $A(0) = 200$; $A(c) = 200 + \int_0^c (E(t) - D(t))\,dt \approx 301.491$; $A(10) = 200 + \int_0^{10} (E(t) - D(t))\,dt \approx 258.324$. The absolute maximum amount of water is about 301.491 liters, at $t \approx 7.041$ hours.
